title: Why not more daughters?
hook: In a group that is 80% female, who has more children on average: a son or a daughter?

knows: every child has one mother and one father
natural selection favours parents who leave more descendants
doesNotKnow: that the rarer sex has more children each
that this pulls the sex ratio toward 50:50 (Fisher's argument)

misconception: Evolution would favour whichever sex ratio makes the population grow fastest (mostly females).
objective: The learner can explain that because every child has one father and one mother, in a population of 8 women and 2 men each man has on average 4 times as many children as each woman, so parents producing the rarer sex gain more grandchildren and the ratio is pulled toward even.

claims.text: Every child has one mother and one father, so all women together and all men together have the same number of children; with 8 women and 2 men sharing 40 children, women average 5 and men 20, a ratio of 4.
claims.source: 40/8 = 5, 40/2 = 20, 20/5 = 4; in general per man / per woman = F/M = 0.8/0.2 = 4 (artifacts/scratch/w2life/check.mjs).

claims.text: Many species produce sons and daughters in roughly equal numbers. Because the rarer sex has more offspring each, parents that produce more of the rarer sex leave more grandchildren, which pulls the sex ratio toward even (Fisher's principle).
claims.source: Fisher R.A. (1930) The Genetical Theory of Natural Selection, Oxford, ch. 6; Hamilton W.D. (1967) Science 156:477-488.

claims.text: With 5 women and 5 men, each has 8 children on average: no advantage to either sex.

Exceptions exist: when brothers compete with each other for mates (local mate competition), selection favours female-biased ratios; the even-ratio argument also assumes sons and daughters cost the same to raise.
claims.source: Hamilton W.D. (1967) Extraordinary sex ratios, Science 156:477-488; Fisher (1930) on equal parental expenditure.

claims.text: The 10 adults and 40 children are made up, and each sex shares its children equally (averages only).
claims.source: Model choice in Demo.tsx, stated in the reveal.

recall.question: In a population with 3 times as many males as females, which offspring gives a parent the most grandchildren on average?
recall.why: Every child has one mother and one father, so the rarer sex (females here) has more children each: a daughter averages 3 times as many as a son.
